simulation_brief.summary: A fictional local rent board is considering a temporary rent cap after a sudden rent spike attributed in part to rising insurance costs. Small landlords claim the cost shock is real, tenants are organizing for relief, insurers are avoiding public comment, and council members want better data before a formal vote.
simulation_brief.t0_conditions: Issue is salient but not yet at maximum crisis. Public contestation is emerging, decision-makers are information-seeking, and formal policy choice remains open.

uncertainties: magnitude of insurance contribution to rent spike
extent of landlord ability to absorb costs
whether council consolidates around temporary cap or delays

sociology_baseline.description: Without fresh conflict, data releases, or visible hardship stories, broader public attention is likely to fade before the formal vote.
Additional renters may participate if early organizing demonstrates turnout and procedural relevance.
Moderates may stay publicly quiet despite private concern due to uncertainty and fear of social or economic exposure.
Actors are more likely to update on evidence framed within existing narratives than on adversarial claims alone.
Information and interpretation cluster within renter and landlord networks.
Visible multiple-source endorsements increase likelihood of broader tenant participation.
Group labels shape perceived legitimacy and grievance interpretation.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Upcoming formal vote creates a focal point for organizing and countermobilization.
Council demand for data slows closure and raises the value of credible evidence.
Insurer refusal to comment creates an information vacuum and suspicion.
Sudden rent increase keeps issue personally salient for affected tenants.
